MICROSOFT VISUAL C++ RUNTIME COMPONENTS — DISTRIBUTABLE CODE NOTICE
===================================================================

This product includes Microsoft Visual C++ runtime components, which are
Microsoft Distributable Code, copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. Microsoft
does not ship a standalone licence text alongside these DLLs; the terms that
authorise their redistribution travel with the upstream distributions that
supplied them, as described below. This notice identifies every such component
in the product, its provenance, and the conditions that apply.

1. COMPONENTS AND PROVENANCE
----------------------------

(a) Supplied as part of the official python.org CPython 3.12 Windows binary
    distribution, and placed in the package by the freeze process:

      _internal/VCRUNTIME140.dll
      _internal/VCRUNTIME140_1.dll
      _internal/ucrtbase.dll
      _internal/api-ms-win-*.dll        (39 API-set forwarder DLLs)

    Authority: the CPython Windows binary distribution is licensed under the
    Python Software Foundation License Version 2 together with the
    "Additional Conditions for this Windows binary build" section of its
    LICENSE.txt, shipped with this product verbatim as
    licenses/CPython-LICENSE.txt. That section states, in Microsoft's and the
    PSF's own words, the conditions under which the Microsoft Distributable
    Code embedded in and accompanying the CPython build may be further
    distributed.

(b) Supplied inside the Qt for Python wheels (PySide6 6.8.1.1 and
    shiboken6 6.8.1.1), exactly as published by The Qt Company on PyPI:

      _internal/PySide6/MSVCP140.dll
      _internal/PySide6/MSVCP140_1.dll
      _internal/PySide6/MSVCP140_2.dll
      _internal/PySide6/VCRUNTIME140.dll
      _internal/PySide6/VCRUNTIME140_1.dll
      _internal/shiboken6/MSVCP140.dll
      _internal/shiboken6/VCRUNTIME140.dll
      _internal/shiboken6/VCRUNTIME140_1.dll

    These files are the same class of Microsoft Distributable Code (Visual
    C++ runtime libraries), redistributed by The Qt Company within its
    published wheels. The wheels do not include a Microsoft-specific licence
    text. This product ships those files unmodified, in the locations the
    wheels place them, and applies to them the same protective conditions
    listed in section 2.

No other Microsoft runtime or redistributable component is included. In
particular, no MSVCR* (legacy CRT), CONCRT*, VCOMP* (OpenMP), MFC or VCAMP
file is shipped, and the product does not install or require the standalone
Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable package.

2. CONDITIONS OF REDISTRIBUTION
-------------------------------

The following conditions are reproduced from the "Additional Conditions for
this Windows binary build" section of licenses/CPython-LICENSE.txt, which is
the authoritative statement accompanying the distribution that supplied the
files in 1(a):

    This program is linked with and uses Microsoft Distributable Code,
    copyrighted by Microsoft Corporation. [...]

    If you further distribute programs that include the Microsoft
    Distributable Code, you must comply with the restrictions on
    distribution specified by Microsoft. In particular, you must require
    distributors and external end users to agree to terms that protect the
    Microsoft Distributable Code at least as much as Microsoft's own
    requirements for the Distributable Code. [...]

    Redistribution of the Windows binary build of the Python interpreter
    complies with this agreement, provided that you do not:

    - alter any copyright, trademark or patent notice in Microsoft's
    Distributable Code;

    - use Microsoft's trademarks in your programs' names or in a way that
    suggests your programs come from or are endorsed by Microsoft;

    - distribute Microsoft's Distributable Code to run on a platform other
    than Microsoft operating systems, run-time technologies or application
    platforms; or

    - include Microsoft Distributable Code in malicious, deceptive or
    unlawful programs.

PreflightQC observes each of those conditions: the files are shipped
unmodified with all notices intact; Microsoft's trademarks appear nowhere in
the product's name or presentation; the product runs only on Microsoft
Windows; and the product inspects media files read-only and does nothing
deceptive or unlawful.

3. END-USER TERMS
-----------------

As required above, the product's licence agreement (EULA) must bind end users
to terms that protect the Microsoft Distributable Code at least as much as
Microsoft's own requirements. Confirming that the EULA wording satisfies this
pass-through obligation — including for the copies that arrive via the Qt for
Python wheels rather than via CPython — is part of the attorney review
recorded as gate G-12 in docs/licensing/LICENSING-GATE-V1.md. That gate
remains open until a qualified attorney completes it; this notice records the
factual basis and does not claim legal clearance.

Reference: Microsoft's current documentation for the Visual C++
redistributable files is published at
https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist
(reference pointer only; nothing is fetched by the product).
